summary: Phase 136R implemented CLTR-CUTOVER-EXECUTABLE-SCHEMAS-001 v1.0's contract Group 8 (Sec.46): ConcurrencyConflict and RecoveryJournalEntry, paired atomically per CSCH-EXEC-REQ-062. Before writing any schema file, independently re-derived Sec.46's group table and found a genuine conflict between this phase's task prompt (which asked for a 'recovery schema' while explicitly excluding ConcurrencyConflict and 'Group 8 schemas') and the frozen contract: Group 9 (ReconciliationResult) has no schema file at all per Sec.29, and Group 11 (QuarantineRecord) depends on Group 8 being complete first per Sec.46, so no contract-conformant recovery schema group excluding ConcurrencyConflict exists -- this is precisely the disposition 136Q's own independent-verification report (Sec.18) had already reached and recommended. Surfaced this conflict to the user before coding and received explicit confirmation to implement Group 8 in full, overriding the prompt's textual exclusion, since the frozen contract governs over prompt text per this phase's own standing instruction. Implemented records/concurrency_conflict.schema.json and records/recovery_journal_entry.schema.json (Tier 2, _extensions only per Sec.14; authority_role 'authoritative' locally forbidden per Sec.9's 12-file list). Neither embeds cas_expectation (Sec.24 names only cutover_candidate/certification/publication_attempt as embedding sites); both reuse only pre-existing shared-core definitions (envelope, identity, digest, enums, references, limitations) and reference only already-existing earlier-group families (cutover_request, authority_state, publication_attempt) -- no cycle exists, and the two Group 8 siblings do not reference each other. RecoveryJournalEntry's hash chain (prior_entry_digest) is null only at sequence==0 and otherwise points strictly backward to the immediately preceding entry's own digest, per Sec.28. Added 2 manifest entries (18 total), each tagged implementation_group 8 -- the true contract group number, disclosed as a deliberate departure from the pre-existing informal per-phase counter used by Groups 3-7's entries (NON-BLOCKING-136R-2), not a repair of those entries. Migrated 12 earlier-phase test files' scope-guard assertions narrowly to recognize the two new files as legitimate while keeping Group 9+ families, ConcurrencyConflict/RecoveryJournalEntry splitting, standalone CASExpectation, bindings, views, typed models, and semantic validators forbidden. Authored a fresh 113-test focused module, tests/test_cltr_cutover_136r_recovery_schema.py: 113/113 passed. Combined Groups 1-8 + schema-runtime suite: 1419/1419 passed. Fast Green: 4391/4391 passed, matching 136Q's own count exactly. Full unmarked suite freshly run (current tree, active 136R task, uncommitted changes at the time of the run): 21477 passed, 20 failed. Built a fresh isolated git worktree at the pre-136R commit (15fca95e, clean checkout, no active task): 21384 passed, 10 failed. Node-ID comparison confirmed zero of the 20 current-tree failures touch cltr_cutover, schema_runtime, publication, concurrency_conflict, recovery_journal_entry, or any 136P/136Q/136R module; only 7 of the 10 baseline failures reappear, and the remaining current-tree failures concern finalization-transaction/migration-evidence/notification-certification behavior sensitive to live governed-lifecycle state -- directly reconfirming NON-BLOCKING-136Q-1's own prediction that the inherited-failure-set composition shifts with live state rather than being a stable frozen node-ID set. Built a fresh wheel and sdist via python -m build; both contain exactly the 11 expected records/*.schema.json files (no Group 9+ file); installed the wheel into a clean isolated virtualenv and validated Group 8 fixtures offline outside the repository checkout. socket.socket/socket.create_connection monkeypatched to raise during registry construction and validation -- zero network calls. No .pcae/cltr-authority/ directory exists; no RecoveryCoordinator/RetryExecutor/PointerRepair/ReconciliationEngine/QuarantineEnforcer/ConflictResolver symbol exists in either new schema file or anywhere in src/. Reviewed and dispositioned all four inherited 136M findings, all eight 136N findings, 136O's two additions, and all four 136Q findings (including NON-BLOCKING-136Q-1, reconfirmed above) -- none converted to Blocking; four new Non-Blocking findings disclosed (NON-BLOCKING-136R-1 through -4: publication_attempt_reference/operator_review/recovery_action gap-fills; the manifest implementation_group labeling departure; several cross-family references left generic where Sec.27/Sec.28 name no specific family; generation_reference typing precedent). Zero Blocking findings; no repair to production schema/manifest content was necessary beyond the two new files themselves. Legacy lifecycle remains the sole production authority; CLTR remains derivative; runtime remains Observed / observe / execution unavailable. No ReconciliationResult, QuarantineRecord, notification/marker/receipt binding, CompatibilityState, HistoricalAuthorityReference, typed model, semantic validator, or authority resolver/state/pointer was created or changed by Phase 136R. Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE, ZERO BLOCKING FINDINGS -- READY FOR RECOVERY SCHEMA INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. Recommended next phase: 136S -- Recovery Schema Independent Verification.
